Q1: Which part of the repository should this issue change?
Choices:
A) The clarify / plan / implement pipeline: the `ai-clarify.yml`, plan and implement workflows and their prompts
B) Review & autofix: `review_autofix.yml`, its reviewer, aggregator and editor modes, and its helper scripts
C) The orchestrator: `orchestrate_poll.yml`, waves, integration-sync and stall recovery
D) Docs only: `README.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md` and `agents.d/` fragments
E) Something else. Name the exact file, workflow or script in your `/answer` (RECOMMENDED)
Q2: What kind of improvement do you want?
Choices:
A) Fix a specific bug or failure. Include the failing run ID, log excerpt or reproduction steps (RECOMMENDED)
B) Cut cost or runtime: fewer tokens, fewer GitHub API calls, faster jobs
C) Make it more reliable: fewer transient failures, better retries and self-healing
D) Make it clearer for operators: better logs, Telegram alerts or docs
E) Add a new feature. Describe the behaviour you want
Q3: How will we know the change is done?
Choices:
A) A specific failing scenario or test now passes. Name it in your `/answer` (RECOMMENDED)
B) A measurable metric reaches a target, such as job duration, token use or failure rate. Give the number
C) A reviewer confirms the behaviour you described in Q2 is in place, with no specific metric
Q4: How large a change is allowed?
Choices:
A) Surgical: the smallest change to the files named in Q1, plus matching contract tests (RECOMMENDED)
B) Moderate: may touch several related workflows or scripts while keeping their behaviour consistent with each other
C) Broad: refactoring or redesigning the named subsystem is allowed
